title: Save the banyan tree
text:
Jalan Kenanga 7
Sumberjaya
East Java

12 September

The Editor
Suara Kota

Dear Editor,

I am writing to ask your readers to help save the great banyan tree in our town square. Your newspaper reported last week that the town council plans to cut it down next month to make room for forty new parking spaces. I believe this would be a terrible mistake.

First of all, the banyan tree is part of our town’s history. It is more than 120 years old, which means it was already growing when my great-grandparents were children. Families have met in its shade for generations, and it appears in old photographs of the square. Once it is gone, we can never get it back.

Secondly, the tree keeps the square cool. On hot afternoons, the air under its branches feels much cooler than the bare pavement around it, and people sit there to rest. Without it, the square would become an uncomfortable patch of hot concrete.

The tree is also home to wildlife. Every evening, hundreds of birds gather noisily in its branches, and fruit bats feed on its figs at night. Where would all these creatures go?

Of course, I understand that drivers need somewhere to park. However, there is an empty piece of land behind the market that could easily become a car park. It is only a five-minute walk from the square.

The council has a simple choice: a few more parking spaces, or a living landmark that has served our town for over a century. I hope that every reader who cares about our town will write to the council before its meeting on 30 September.

Yours faithfully,

Intan Permata (aged 11)
